items.title: Dave McKenna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I had a little kid, a baby boy, Steve

ctx.x: Okay, that’s what I was going to say — is there a stretch of years that music has been the toughest for you?

That was it. I was living in New York in a walk-up and I was working at Eddie Condon’s. I think the base pay was $150 a week, and it took $25 out of the income, and I think the rent in that walk-up was about a hundred thirty something, and I had a little kid, a baby boy, Steve, and it was tight. I got a few extras but, you see the guys that worked Condon’s, like Yank and all those guys, some of them were on staff, and they did this to play music, but they had salaries. But I wasn’t on staff. Although Bobby…
That sounds like it’d be pretty tight to live in New York on that kind of base pay I guess.
